description: Hardening fixture rows for integrateViewOpticalDepth. These rows pin packet ownership, diagnostic semantics, and sourced positive/negative extreme families before implementation.

expectedComparisonPolicy.nonnumeric: Exact structural comparison for object, array, string, boolean, and null expected values. Numeric optical-depth and transmittance values use each datum's tolerance rule.

reference.title: Reference Code Design
reference.locator: integrateViewOpticalDepth Output Shape, path-end diagnostic paragraph.
reference.derivationSummary: The selected path end is the final interval endpoint, not the final midpoint sample distance, because midpoint samples are integrand evaluation positions.

assumptions.pathSamples: one midpoint sample with an explicit finite interval endpoint

pathEndDistanceKm.derivation: Local packet contract: the final sample's finite intervalEndKm is 3 km, so pathEnd.distanceFromObserverKm is 3 km.

expectations.independence: This is a local packet-shape oracle backed by the stage output contract, not by current implementation fallback behavior.

reference.title: Reference Code Design
reference.locator: integrateViewOpticalDepth Output Shape, open follow-up decisions.
reference.derivationSummary: Downstream diagnostics need finite path distances; non-finite endpoints cannot represent a physical transport segment.

assumptions.invalidReason: final intervalEndKm is an encoded non-finite sentinel

expectedError.derivation: A non-finite final interval endpoint is not a valid kilometer distance for camera-to-end diagnostics.

expectations.independence: The invalid endpoint is fixture-owned malformed data, not an implementation-generated value.

reference.title: Reference Code Design
reference.locator: Stage Boundary Ownership and integrateViewOpticalDepth Output Shape.
reference.derivationSummary: Sample weights and interval endpoints are owned by mediumSamples/sampleViewPath; viewOpticalDepth carries transport diagnostics derived from those samples.

canonicalGeometryOwner.derivation: The fixture expects later consumers to read sample geometry from mediumSamples, with viewOpticalDepth storing derived transport diagnostics only.

viewOpticalDepthRequiredFields.derivation: The required viewOpticalDepth sample fields identify sample index/distance and transport diagnostics used downstream.

expectations.independence: The expected ownership is stated by the design contract so future code cannot create parallel sources of geometry truth.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
reference.locator: Optical depth as the path integral of extinction.
reference.derivationSummary: Species optical depth accumulates along the path just like total optical depth; for two 1 km samples at 0.1/km and 0.2/km, cumulative tau is 0.1 then 0.3.

rayleighCumulativeTauBySample.derivation: PBRT optical-depth integral by sample: first cumulative tau = 0.1*1 = 0.1; second cumulative tau = 0.1 + 0.2*1 = 0.3.

expectations.independence: The expected cumulative values are hand-derived from species extinction and sample weights.

reference.title: CIE 1931 colour-matching functions, 2 degree observer
reference.locator: Dataset description and metadata: 360-830 nm, 1 nm wavelength steps, md5 checksum, DOI 10.25039/CIE.DS.xvudnb9b.
reference.derivationSummary: The official CIE metadata gives wavelength_first 360, wavelength_last 830, wavelength_step 1, and checksum 17cca777db64b17170f06f67ce9d3ab7. Inclusive count is 830 - 360 + 1 = 471.

assumptions.gridPurpose: visible-spectrum alignment stress for wavelength-indexed arrays

gridMetadata.derivation: CIE metadata states 360-830 nm at 1 nm increments; inclusive row count is 471.

checksumMd5.derivation: CIE dataset page and metadata list this md5 checksum for CIE_xyz_1931_2deg.csv.

expectations.independence: The expected grid shape and checksum come from the official CIE dataset metadata, not a local generated grid helper.

reference.title: CIE 1931 colour-matching functions, 2 degree observer
reference.locator: Dataset metadata: 360-830 nm, 1 nm steps, md5 checksum, DOI 10.25039/CIE.DS.xvudnb9b.
reference.derivationSummary: The sourced visible grid has 471 wavelength samples, so coefficient arrays with 470 entries, 472 entries, or scalar collapse cannot align one-to-one.

expectedError.derivation: A 471-row sourced grid requires exactly 471 coefficient entries. Scalar, short, or long arrays cannot be interpreted without an interpolation/broadcast policy.

expectations.independence: The invalid array lengths are derived from the CIE metadata count and the local spectral-array contract.

expectations.quantity: ASTM G-173 wavelength-grid positive alignment extreme

reference.title: NLR Reference Air Mass 1.5 Spectra, ASTM G-173
reference.locator: Data Files section for the ASTM G-173 tables; table fields list wavelength in nanometers and spectral irradiance columns.
reference.derivationSummary: The NLR ASTM G-173 data table is a wavelength-indexed spectral dataset. The inspected ASTMG173.csv provenance records 2002 rows from 280 nm to 4000 nm with nonuniform spacing.

assumptions.sourceFile: ASTMG173.csv from NLR compressed data file

gridMetadata.derivation: NLR provides the ASTM G-173 wavelength-indexed data table; local inspected data provenance records ASTMG173.csv with 2002 rows from 280 nm to 4000 nm.

downloadedCsvChecksum.derivation: Reference Test Design records the inspected downloaded ASTMG173.csv checksums for local provenance.

expectations.independence: The expected grid extent/count/checksum come from the NLR data file provenance, not from a generated wavelength loop.

expectations.quantity: ASTM G-173 wavelength-grid negative alignment extreme

reference.title: NLR Reference Air Mass 1.5 Spectra, ASTM G-173
reference.locator: Data Files section for ASTM G-173 tables and table-field description.
reference.derivationSummary: The inspected NLR ASTMG173.csv grid has 2002 wavelength rows. A coefficient array must align one-to-one with the active grid and cannot be scalar-collapsed or off by one.

expectedError.derivation: The NLR data provenance gives 2002 wavelength rows; coefficient arrays with any other count cannot align to that table.

expectations.independence: The invalid shapes are derived from the sourced ASTM table count and the spectral-array contract.

expectations.quantity: sourced clear-air Rayleigh optical-depth positive extreme

reference.title: Bucholtz 1995, Rayleigh-scattering calculations for the terrestrial atmosphere
reference.locator: Table 4, Rayleigh optical depth for named standard atmospheres.
reference.derivationSummary: Bucholtz Table 4 gives a 1962 U.S. Standard atmosphere Rayleigh optical depth of 8.645e-3 at 1.00 um. This is a data row, not a local wavelength-power-law calculation.

inputs.pathModel: vertical column optical depth already supplied from Bucholtz table

rayleighTauByWavelength.derivation: Bucholtz Table 4 row: 1962 U.S. Standard atmosphere, wavelength 1.00 um, Rayleigh optical depth tau = 8.645e-3.

expectations.independence: The expected optical depth is copied from the published table row; no local Rayleigh formula or coefficient generator is used.

expectations.quantity: sourced clear-air optical-depth negative provenance check

reference.title: Reference Test Design
reference.locator: Expected Value Policy and integrateViewOpticalDepth hardening inventory.
reference.derivationSummary: Clear-air optical-depth fixtures must pin source, atmosphere model, wavelength, and coefficient assumptions before they can become expected data.

assumptions.invalidReason: missing atmosphere/model/source assumptions for a claimed clear-air optical-depth extreme

candidateFixture.description: generic clear sky is very optically thin

expectedError.derivation: A claimed Earth clear-air optical-depth extreme without pinned source/model assumptions is not a defensible fixture oracle.

expectations.independence: The rejection is based on provenance policy, preventing a locally invented 'looks plausible' optical-depth limit.

reference.title: Kasten and Young 1989, Revised optical air mass tables and approximation formula
reference.locator: Table II, optical air mass rows for low solar elevation.
reference.derivationSummary: Kasten and Young Table II gives horizon elevation 0.0 deg as relative optical air mass 38.0868 and absolute optical air mass 394428 kg/m2. Use this only when the test adopts the same air-mass convention.

assumptions.airMassConvention: Kasten and Young optical air mass table
assumptions.pathUse: path sanity fixture, not generic flat-world multiplier

airMassRow.derivation: Kasten and Young Table II row: elevation 0.0 deg, relative optical air mass 38.0868, absolute optical air mass 394428 kg/m2.

expectations.independence: The expected values are table rows from Kasten and Young, not a local air-mass approximation formula.

reference.title: Reference Test Design
reference.locator: Air-Mass Path Checks and Flat Large-Lateral-Path Checks.
reference.derivationSummary: Near-horizon or slant-path tests must adopt a named air-mass/path convention. Arbitrary path multipliers are rejected because they hide geometry assumptions.

expectedError.derivation: A slant multiplier chosen without a cited table or declared geometry cannot be used as expected data.

expectations.independence: The negative fixture prevents arbitrary horizon constants from entering the reference.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
reference.locator: Homogeneous Beer-Lambert transmittance over a finite segment.
reference.derivationSummary: When a flat-world model supplies a finite named lateral boundary, homogeneous optical depth is still tau = sigma_t * lateralDistance and T = exp(-tau).

supportingReferences.title: Reference Code Design
supportingReferences.locator: Model Interface and flat/local-Sun boundary contract.
supportingReferences.supports: The finite lateral boundary is a model-owned hypothesis, not an integration cap.

assumptions.geometryHypothesis: finite named flat local patch boundary

tauByWavelength.derivation: PBRT homogeneous Beer-Lambert over a finite named segment: tau = 0.02 / km * 10 km = 0.2.

expectations.independence: The numeric optical-depth expectation is analytic; the finite lateral distance is an explicitly named fixture hypothesis, not a hidden renderer cap.

reference.title: Reference Code Design
reference.locator: Flat/local-Sun model contract and Error Handling.
reference.derivationSummary: A flat horizontal slab path is infinite without a named lateral boundary. Hiding that as a numerical cap would turn a model assumption into a magic number.

assumptions.invalidReason: unbounded flat path represented as an integration cap

expectedError.derivation: The model must provide a named finite lateral boundary before optical-depth integration can proceed.

expectations.independence: The negative fixture blocks arbitrary flat-world path caps from becoming transport constants.

reference.title: Reference Code Design
reference.locator: evaluateMedium Output Shape and integrateViewOpticalDepth Output Shape.
reference.derivationSummary: Until the first clear-air coefficient model is selected, species-count extremes are model-schema fixtures. The current clear-air candidate set is Rayleigh, aerosol/Mie, and absorber/ozone.

assumptions.selectedModelStatus: candidate schema, not final coefficient model

speciesNames.derivation: The fixture's selected-model candidate schema has three named species/components that must remain separately diagnosable.

totalTauByWavelength.derivation: Species optical depths add for one 1 km sample: 0.1 + 0.02 + 0.003 = 0.123.

expectations.independence: The species names are a local model-schema candidate and the total is hand-derived from fixture-owned coefficients.

reference.title: Reference Code Design
reference.locator: evaluateMedium Output Shape and integrateViewOpticalDepth Output Shape.
reference.derivationSummary: Species diagnostics must remain wavelength-aligned; mismatched arrays cannot be attributed downstream.

invalidReasons: coefficient array length does not match wavelengthsNm

expectedError.derivation: One coefficient cannot represent two active wavelengths for the named species.

expectations.independence: The invalid species rows are fixture-owned schema violations, not implementation-specific edge cases.

reference.title: Future convergence study for selected reference profile
reference.locator: Placeholder row to be replaced by a checked-in convergence-study artifact.
reference.derivationSummary: This row records the required fixture shape, but the expected sample count and error bound are not source-backed yet. Do not enable it until an external-tool or independent convergence artifact is checked in.

expectedError.derivation: No positive max-sample-count fixture can be enabled until a convergence artifact pins the selected profile, reference solution, and tolerance.

expectations.independence: This row intentionally blocks implementation based on an unsourced sample-count maximum.

reference.title: Reference Test Design
reference.derivationSummary: Sample-count limits are numerical evidence, not physical constants. They need a convergence study rather than an arbitrary maximum.

assumptions.invalidReason: max sample count selected by preference rather than convergence evidence

expectedError.derivation: A sample-count extreme must cite convergence evidence; otherwise it is an arbitrary implementation limit.

expectations.independence: The row rejects an unsourced numerical cap rather than making it a package contract.
